title: AWS CDK Advanced
description: Build reusable infrastructure with AWS CDK constructs, custom constructs, and CDK Pipelines.

data.text: The **AWS Cloud Development Kit (CDK)** lets you define cloud infrastructure using familiar programming languages like TypeScript, Python, or Java. Instead of writing YAML or JSON, you write code that describes your infrastructure.

A **construct** is a building block representing an AWS resource or a group of resources. Constructs range from low-level (L1, mapping directly to CloudFormation resources) to high-level (L2 and L3, with sensible defaults and helper methods).

data.title: Custom CDK Construct in TypeScript
data.content: This TypeScript example shows a custom construct that creates an S3 bucket with a lifecycle policy.

data.text: **CDK Pipelines** is a construct library that sets up a complete continuous delivery pipeline for your CDK apps. It uses AWS CodePipeline under the hood and can deploy across multiple stages and accounts.

terms.definition: A basic building block in CDK representing AWS resources.
A collection of constructs that defines a unit of deployment.
The top-level container for one or more stacks.
A higher-level construct for setting up CI/CD pipelines.

data.title: Exercise: Build a Custom Construct
data.description: Create a custom CDK construct that provisions a Lambda function with a REST API endpoint and appropriate IAM permissions.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: CDK lets you write infrastructure as code in familiar languages
CDK Pipelines automates deployment with CodePipeline
